task:
Analyze the Jellyfin.PreTranscode plugin codebase for UI redesign planning. Focus on:
1. Technology stack and versions (C#, Jellyfin SDK, JavaScript)
2. Current UI structure (list.html) - how it works, limitations
3. Plugin architecture - how config pages work, how to add dashboard cards
4. Existing patterns for: notifications, scheduling, API endpoints
5. Relevant file paths for UI changes
6. How Jellyfin's native CSS/JS components work in plugins

criteria.must: Return concrete findings with file paths and severity when applicable
Return concrete findings with file paths and severity when applicable

criteriaSatisfied.evidence: All findings include specific file paths (e.g., Configuration/list.html, Controllers/PreTranscodeController.cs, Plugin.cs), concrete technology versions (.NET 9.0, Jellyfin 10.11.11, LiteDB 5.0.21), and severity notes for UI limitations. 6 major file paths identified for UI changes. API endpoints, component patterns, and notification options documented with code examples.

validationOutput: Research cross-verified against: csproj (versions), Plugin.cs (IHasWebPages), list.html (UI structure), PreTranscodeController.cs (API), JobQueueService.cs (jobs), PreTranscodeTask.cs (scheduling), ui-redesign-requirements.md (known issues), Jellyfin Plugin SDK KB (patterns), Jellyfin Source Code KB (interfaces)
residualRisks: No native Jellyfin API for dashboard home cards - plugins only get sidebar menu pages
GPU usage monitoring requires system-level access not available in plugin sandbox
Current job progress is file-size based and approximate - not frame/time accurate
Jellyfin 10.11.11 API lock - future version upgrades may require changes
reviewFindings: info: Configuration/list.html - 22KB single file with ~80% inline CSS, needs cleanup
info: Configuration/configPage.html - exists but NOT registered in Plugin.GetPages(), orphaned file
info: Plugin.cs - only exposes list.html, no separate settings page registered
info: Controllers/PreTranscodeController.cs - 4 endpoints, all properly authorized
info: Services/JobQueueService.cs - progress via file size comparison, no encoder telemetry
info: No notification system implemented - IActivityManager/INotificationManager not injected
info: ScheduledTasks/PreTranscodeTask.cs - no default triggers configured (empty array)
childReport.manualNotes: Key insight: Jellyfin plugins do NOT have a native dashboard card API. The 'dashboard home card' requirement from ui-redesign-requirements.md would require either (a) using Activity Log as a proxy, (b) WebSocket-based real-time updates to the plugin page, or (c) modifying jellyfin-web directly. The current list.html is functional but heavily uses inline CSS and pseudo-Jellyfin card classes without proper structure. The configPage.html file is orphaned - it exists as an embedded resource but is never served because Plugin.GetPages() only returns list.html.
